subject: Clarify flexible-tier upgrade path and feature bundle tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sophia Holt <sophia.holt@pulsehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options — upgrade path + bundling questions

Hi Logan / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to deciding whether to move PulseHealth from the Compact tier to something more elastic to cover our anticipated Q3 usage spike. A few concrete questions from the procurement and engineering teams so we can put together an internal recommendation: 

- If we upgrade mid-term from Compact -> Elastic (12k reqs/day to expected 45k/day), how do proration and credits work? Do we get pro-rated credits for unused Compact commitment and how are overage rates applied during the first full billing month after upgrade?
- We're interested in the "Optimize" feature bundle you showed (auto-batching + prefix caching + model quantization recommendations). Can that be add-on only for a subset of routes (e.g., clinical-summary pipeline) or is it all-or-nothing at account level?
- What discount levels are available for a 12-month committed Elastic reservation vs month-to-month? Procurement is pushing for a 10%+ discount to offset integration costs.

Attached: current usage export and the MAAP (security) PDF procurement asked for.

We can do a quick call tomorrow morning PST to walk through, or if you could send a short options matrix that lays out prices, proration behavior, and recommended rollout (canary -> full), that would be helpful.

Best,
Sophia Holt
Director of Engineering Operations
PulseHealth

Attachments: PulseHealth_current_usage_export.csv (CSV, 12 KB), PulseHealth_MAAP_v2.pdf (PDF, 680 KB)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Holt <sophia.holt@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — upgrade path + bundling questions

Hi Sophia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and then a proposed options matrix (attached). I'll call out the operational impact so you can pass to procurement/eng: 

Summary answers:
- Proration and credits: we pro-rate the remaining unused portion of your Compact reservation and apply it as account credit at the time the Elastic reservation is activated. Example (very condensed): if you pre-paid 6 months of Compact and upgrade at month 3, the remaining 3-month value is converted to a credit applied to the new Elastic invoice. Overage behavior during the transition month uses Elastic overage rates; we'll cap your per-token price to the higher of Compact's committed unit price and Elastic's overage price for the first billing cycle to avoid big spikes.

- Optimize bundle scoping: Optimize can be scoped by route. You can enable auto-batching + prefix caching for only the clinical-summary route while leaving other routes on standard settings. Quantization/model-recommendation actions require a short integration review but can also be targeted to specific models.

- Discounting: standard list is 0% for month-to-month, 7.5% for 12-month Elastic with a 6-month ramp, and 12% for 12-month Elastic with an immediate commit. Given PulseHealth's size and the Q3 runway you described, we can consider an additional concession: 10% + a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 6 weeks of Dedicated onboarding support) if you sign a 12-month immediate commit. Ben and Marissa are looped on this.

Attached is a short options matrix:
1) Elastic immediate-commit (12mo) — 12% discount, route-scoped Optimize add-on priced per-route, includes 6 weeks onboarding credit if you take the concession (see DEAL-15892 special).
2) Elastic ramp (12mo with 6mo ramp) — 7.5% discount, smaller onboarding credit, flexible seat scaling.
3) Temporary burst + metered (month-to-month) — no discount, fast to enable, good for short spikes but higher unit costs and no onboarding package.

Next steps: happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow 9:30–10:30am PST. If procurement prefers, we'll put the concession scenario into a formal quote and DocuSign draft after we confirm expected concurrency and peak token/sec.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0163

Attachments: pricing-breakdown.xlsx (Excel, 38 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Packaging options — upgrade path + bundling questions

Quick internal — copying here to keep a record: 

If PulseHealth is willing to sign a 12mo immediate commit, suggest we offer:
- 10% list discount (match procurement ask) + 6 weeks onboarding credit (as Logan noted) rather than 12% so we keep margin headroom.
- Include Optimize for one route (clinical-summary) at 50% off for the first 3 months so they can validate cost/perf improvements.
- Offer a one-time observability retention bump (30 days -> 90 days) as a low-cost value-add to sweeten the negotiation.

Reasons: gives procurement the number they want, lets engineering trial Optimize without full account rollout, and preserves ability to upsell once we show cost savings. I can be on the procurement call if needed.

-Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Sophia Holt <sophia.holt@pulsehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — upgrade path + bundling questions

Logan / Ben — thanks, that helps a lot.

PulseHealth procurement is comfortable with the 10% concession + onboarding credit and the route-scoped Optimize trial for clinical-summary. Can you: 

1) Send a formal quote that shows proration examples and the one-time credits (we need this for internal approval).
2) Mark up DocuSign with DEAL-15892 and the concession terms so procurement can circulate.

We will plan for a short integration pilot starting mid-May (target May 15) to validate the Optimize gains before the Q3 ramp. We have an NDA addendum request (small change to data-retention clause) — I'll attach to the DocuSign packet.

Let me know if you want a synchronous call; procurement says asynchronous is fine if the quote + DocuSign arrive today.

Best,
Sophia
Director of Engineering Operations, PulseHealth

Attachments: (will append NDA addendum in DocuSign)
